item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
135
ABPZ20 KNHC 230520
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, about 200 miles offshore of southern Mexico, and on Tropical
Storm Odalys, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
Baja California.

Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical
Depression Fifteen-E, located a few hundred miles south-southeast
the Big Island of Hawaii, have become better organized.
Environmental conditions remain conducive for development, and a
tropical depression could form tonight or Wednesday while the system
moves slowly west-northwestward. Heavy rains associated with this
system are forecast to spread over the southeastern Hawaiian Islands
starting on Wednesday and continuing through Saturday, possibly
resulting in life-threatening flash flooding and mudslides for
portions of the Big Island and Maui. Interests in the Hawaiian
Islands should continue to monitor the progress of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in a couple of days to
the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterwards, environmental
conditions should be favorable for gradual development, and a
tropical depression is likely to form late this week or this weekend
as the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward,
parallel to the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

...ODALYS FORECAST TO BECOME A HURRICANE LATER TONIGHT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.5N 129.0W
ABOUT 1345 MI...2165 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ENE OR 70 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Odalys was 
located near latitude 15.5 North, longitude 129.0 West. Odalys is 
moving toward the east-northeast near 9 mph (15 km/h). An eastward 
to east-northeastward motion at a slightly slower speed is expected 
through the next couple of days, followed by a gradual turn toward 
the northeast then north later this week. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 70 mph (110 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Additional strengthening is expected, and Odalys is forecast 
to become a hurricane later tonight. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles (240 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 230242
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Odalys Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
800 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026
 
Odalys appears to have been impacted by mid-level dry air 
entrainment earlier tonight, which disrupted the deep convection 
that had been occurring near and to the west of the partially 
exposed center. In addition, a recent SSMIS pass indicated moderate 
northerly wind shear had displaced the mid-level center to the south 
of the low-level circulation and was displacing the remaining 
convection to the south and east of the center. However, new 
convection is developing near the core of Odalys, with cloud top 
temperatures rapidly cooling to below -80 C. The latest TAFB 
intensity estimate was 3.5/55 kt, while objective intensity 
estimates range from 53-67 kt. The intensity is held at 60 kt for 
this advisory. 

The strong tropical storm is moving toward the east-northeast around 
8 kt, and this motion is expected to continue over the next couple 
of days as the system is guided by a strong long-wave trough over 
the far eastern Pacific. The latest NHC forecast has been nudged 
slightly to the left through the first 24 h. A turn toward the 
northeast, followed by a northward motion, is forecast by late this 
week as an upper-level low strengthens and approaches Odalys from 
the northwest. Beyond 72 h, the track forecast becomes more 
uncertain, as a potential interaction with Hurricane Polo could 
influence Odalys' motion while the major hurricane moves parallel to 
the southwestern coast of Mexico. The updated NHC forecast has been 
adjusted to the right of the previous forecast beyond 48 h, toward 
the HCCA solution. 

Weakening wind shear and sufficiently warm sea surface temperatures 
should support gradual strengthening over the next 24 h or so, and 
Odalys is expected to become a hurricane later tonight. By late this 
week, however, increasing wind shear, cooler waters and increasingly 
unfavorable upper-level outflow associated with Hurricane Polo are 
expected to induce gradual weakening through this weekend. The 
current NHC intensity forecast lies near the top of the model 
guidance envelope and remains close to the HCCA and Google DeepMind 
solutions.

item.title: Hurricane Polo Public Advisory Number 10a
item.description:
Issued at 1200 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 230545
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Intermediate Advisory Number 10A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
1200 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026
 
...CATEGORY 5 POLO STATIONARY OFF THE COAST OF SOUTHWESTERN 
MEXICO...

 
SUMMARY OF 1200 AM CST...0600 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.8N 101.2W
ABOUT 200 MI...325 KM S OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
ABOUT 355 MI...570 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...165 MPH...270 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...STATIONARY
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...905 MB...26.73 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Tecpan de Galeana to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* West of Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere along the southwestern Mexico coast should
continue to monitor the progress of this system as additional
watches and warnings could be necessary later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 AM CST (0600 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Polo was located 
near latitude 14.8 North, longitude 101.2 West. Polo is stationary, 
but a sharp turn to the northwest is expected to begin later today 
followed by a general west-northwestward motion later this week and 
over the weekend. On the forecast track, the core of Polo is 
expected to be near the coast of southwestern Mexico during the next 
day or two, although it is forecast to remain offshore.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 165 mph (270 km/h) with higher
gusts. Polo is a category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in intensity are expected, but 
Polo is expected to remain a very powerful major hurricane during 
the next few days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105
miles (165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 905 mb (26.73 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the warning
area along the coast of Mexico later today. Tropical storm
conditions are possible within the watch area along the coast of
Mexico on Thursday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 3 to 6
inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 8 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero and Michoacán through
Thursday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain. Rainfall of 2 to 4
inches is possible in coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima, and
Jalisco through Thursday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Polo are expected to affect portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico during the next few days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf, rip current
conditions, and coastal flooding. Please consult products from
your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 230253
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
900 PM CST Tue Sep 22 2026
 
The last few fixes this afternoon from the NOAA P-3 Hurricane Hunter 
aircraft suggested that Polo was in the middle of an eyewall 
replacement cycle (ERC). Flight level winds from the inner eyewall 
had been decreasing in addition to rising pressures and somewhat 
less pronounced warm core in the center. The secondary eyewall was 
also seen on polar-orbiter imagery with a much larger eyewall taking 
shape on both the SSMIS and WSFM microwave passes compared to this 
morning. The satellite structure of Polo also looks less pristine 
due to the ongoing ERC, with some erosion and expansion of the cold 
cloud tops that surround the eye. Based on the earlier aircraft data 
and evolution of satellite imagery since that time, the initial 
intensity is being set at 145 kt this advisory, still making Polo a 
very dangerous category 5 hurricane.
 
One-minute mesosector imagery over Polo has been very useful to 
monitor its motion, and the inner eye of the storm has been 
wobbling, with the best guess motion an northeastward drift at 45 
degrees at 1 kt. The track guidance remains insistent that Polo will 
soon undergo a slow but sharp turn to the northwest and 
west-northwest as a deep-layer ridge centered over east Texas 
continues to build in. In fact, the track guidance this cycle shows 
even more of a leftward bend in 48-72 h as the ridge moves westward 
with the hurricane. While the latest NHC track forecast is very 
close to the prior one for the first 36 h, it is a little slower 
given the current motion, and then further south and west beyond 36 
h. This track will still take Polo close to, but just offshore of 
the southwestern Mexican coast, where tropical storm conditions are 
still expected. The latest NHC forecast lies closest to the Google 
DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI). Toward the end of the forecast 
period, the ridge steering Polo is forecast to become eroded by a 
combination of Tropical Storm Odalys located to its west, and a 
digging mid-latitude trough moving into the western United States 
coast. Thus, Polo will likely turn back northwestward or even 
northward by the end of the forecast period, though this has also 
been shifted west of the prior track following the leftward shift in 
the guidance this cycle. There still remains significant uncertainty 
in Polo's track in the 4-5 day period.
 
Environmental conditions remain very favorable over Polo currently.
Vertical wind shear is forecast to remain below 10 kt for the next
24 h, with plenty of nearby deep-layer moisture. In addition, Polo
is over the warmest sea-surface temperatures in the basin, which
also extend vertically well below the surface, which should limit
ocean upwelling of the slow moving hurricane. However, the big
question mark is how the ongoing ERC will evolve in the next    
12-24 h. The last few microwave images already show a larger closed
eyewall taking shape. There are also hints of the ERC successfully
completing in the next 24 h in the most recent raw output from the
18z HAFS-A run. Thus, the NHC intensity forecast shows some
short-term fluctuations in intensity both down and up over the next
24-36 h, though it is difficult to forecast these inner-core
structural changes with much confidence. SHIPS guidance thereafter
continues to indicate an increase in easterly shear as the ridging
overhead intensifies, and the NHC intensity forecast shows gradual
weakening beginning by that time, with a somewhat faster rate of
weakening now shown in days 4-5. However, this intensity forecast
remains on the high side of the guidance except for the HFIP
Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA), which is a good 20-30 kt
higher than the rest of the guidance this cycle.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions
of southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
2. A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for portions of
southwestern Mexico, and the Tropical Storm Watch is in effect
westward to Playa Perula. Interests in these areas should closely
monitor updates to the forecast.
